E.ON and enviaM partner with NEURA on a 2027 grid robotics pilot

The partners plan staff-led task design, RoboGym training and later testing at MITNETZ STROM.

E.ON ↗5 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A grid-focused partnership

E.ON, enviaM and NEURA Robotics announced a partnership on November 5 covering energy-infrastructure inspection, monitoring and site tasks. It targets repetitive, strenuous or hazardous work. The announcement describes development and preparation for trials, rather than an established operational fleet.

Training before field trials

Grid staff will help define workflows before controlled training at TUM RoboGym in Munich. The approach combines human-motion data, teleoperation, simulation and real-robot interaction. Testing on enviaM subsidiary MITNETZ STROM’s network is planned for 2027.

Data control and open questions

E.ON and enviaM say they will control their data and trained skills, including decisions about sharing. The development is a utility-specific application of the training infrastructure previously announced at RoboGym. Fleet size, field results and a network-wide rollout schedule remain unspecified.
